## Setup

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

load(url(
  "https://www.openintro.org/data/rda/evals.rda"
))
```

# Exercises

## Exercise 1: Start with the simple relationship

```{r}
ggplot(
  evals,
  aes(x = bty_avg, y = score)
) +
  geom_jitter(
    width = 0,
    height = 0.05,
    alpha = 0.40
  ) +
  geom_smooth(
    method = "lm",
    formula = y ~ x,
    se = FALSE
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Average attractiveness rating",
    y = "Average evaluation score",
    title = "Professor evaluations and attractiveness ratings"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

Describe the direction and strength of the relationship.

> 

Why is `geom_jitter()` useful here?

> 

Does the graph establish causation? Explain.

> 

## Exercise 2: Simple regression

```{r}
m1 <- lm(
  score ~ bty_avg,
  data = evals
)

summary(m1)
```

Write the fitted regression equation.

> 

Interpret the coefficient on `bty_avg`.

> 

What might this simple model be leaving out?

> 

## Exercise 3: Add gender

```{r}
m2 <- lm(
  score ~ bty_avg + gender,
  data = evals
)

summary(m2)
```

What happened to the coefficient on `bty_avg` after adding gender?

> 

Interpret the `bty_avg` coefficient using **holding gender constant**.

> 

Why can coefficients change when another predictor is added?

> 

## Exercise 4: Categorical predictor

```{r}
levels(evals$gender)
```

Which gender is the reference category?

> 

Interpret `gendermale` beginning with:

**Holding attractiveness rating constant...**

> 

Why is this still not a causal statement?

> 

## Exercise 5: Predicted values

```{r}
professors <- data.frame(
  bty_avg = c(5, 5),
  gender = c("female", "male")
)

professors |>
  mutate(
    predicted_score = predict(
      m2,
      newdata = professors
    )
  )
```

What is being held constant?

> 

What differs between the two cases?

> 

Report and interpret the predicted scores.

> 

How does the difference relate to the `gendermale` coefficient?

> 

## Exercise 6: More than two categories

```{r}
levels(evals$rank)

m3 <- lm(
  score ~ bty_avg + rank,
  data = evals
)

summary(m3)
```

How many rank categories are there?

> 

How many rank coefficients appear?

> 

Which category is the reference group?

> 

Interpret one rank coefficient.

> 

Interpret the `bty_avg` coefficient in this model.

> 

## Exercise 7: Add age

```{r}
m4 <- lm(
  score ~ bty_avg + gender + age,
  data = evals
)

summary(m4)
```

Compare the attractiveness coefficient:

```{r}
data.frame(
  model = c(
    "Beauty only",
    "Beauty + gender",
    "Beauty + gender + age"
  ),
  bty_coefficient = c(
    coef(m1)["bty_avg"],
    coef(m2)["bty_avg"],
    coef(m4)["bty_avg"]
  )
)
```

How does the `bty_avg` coefficient change?

> 

Interpret `bty_avg` in `m4`.

> 

Interpret the coefficient on `age`.

> 

Why do you need to know what else is in the model before interpreting a coefficient?

> 

## Exercise 8: Compare profiles

```{r}
profiles <- data.frame(
  bty_avg = c(5, 5, 5),
  gender = c("female", "male", "female"),
  age = c(40, 40, 55)
)

profiles |>
  mutate(
    predicted_score = predict(
      m4,
      newdata = profiles
    )
  )
```

Compare Professors 1 and 2. What is held constant and what changes?

> 

Compare Professors 1 and 3. What is held constant and what changes?

> 

Connect each predicted difference to the appropriate coefficient.

>
